relevance_note: This is a review of genetic predisposition to Behcet's disease that discusses HA20 only at disease level ("a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene") and describes no individual carrying a TNFAIP3 variant.
method_note: Read the full Markdown text (no Supplementary material section is present; the file ends with Associated Data). The paper is a narrative review of genes causing BD-like phenotypes. Table 1 lists PID-related genes, diseases and inheritance, not patients, so it yields no patient rows and contains no stacked ' / ' patient cells; its multi-line gene cell 'NEMO\n \n(IKBKG)' is a gene name, not patient data. The only individual patients described in the text are previously published cases whose variants are in other genes (LIG4, WDR1, NCF1, STAT1, ADA2, AP1S3, LYN, NEMO, RELA, NFKB1, TNFRSF1A, MEFV) and who have no TNFAIP3 variant or HA20 diagnosis; under the scope rule they are out of scope and get no rows. No person with a TNFAIP3 variant or an HA20 diagnosis is described at any individual level, so reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant is false and the individuals, variants, phenotypic_features and phenotype_checklist tables are empty. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients was left null because the paper has no patients of its own and makes no such statement; no cohort size is stated. No contradictions were found.

study_type.span: In this review, we summarize genetic predisposition to BD.
